notes: No fact type in this registry encodes a professional or manufacturing threshold — every 'meaning' describes a geometric measurement or a structural presence/absence check only.

forgeConsumptionStatus is 'not_consumed' for every fact as of Sprint 14: Forge's real rule engine (backend/jewelmind/validation/engine.py) does not yet read GeometricFact objects — see docs/bible/16-geometry-inspection/487-forge-fact-contract.md for the kernel-neutral contract this registry establishes for a future integration, and 494-current-runtime-inspection-gap-analysis.md for why the wiring itself was not done this Sprint (a deliberate, documented scope boundary, not an oversight).

The 6 STONE_REQUESTED_*/STONE_MEASURED_* facts (Sprint 18) deliberately pair a CONSTRUCTION_PARAMETER with an independently MEASURED_GEOMETRY counterpart so an accidental scaling or shape regression is observable as a divergence between them — compared with a software geometry tolerance, never a professional or manufacturing tolerance. See docs/bible/20-stone/574-stone-inspection-contract.md.

STONE_MEASURED_LENGTH/WIDTH derive from an axis-aligned bounding box, so they isolate LENGTH from WIDTH exactly only at stone.orientation == 0. This is a real, documented limitation of the current measurement, not an assumed exactness for every orientation.

The 8 SETTING_*/BEZEL_* facts (Sprint 19) report what the Setting System built and which recorded compatibility status applies. SETTING_COMPATIBILITY_STATUS and BEZEL_WALL_CONTINUOUS are deliberately NOT quality judgements: the first echoes the capability registry, the second is pure topology. Professional interpretation belongs to Forge/Professional Validation (SETTING-GOV-016). Prong-only facts are emitted only for the prong family and bezel-only facts only for bezel, so a fact's presence is itself honest about what was generated.
